correctness.rationale: For G_n=K_{n,n} minus its matching and n≥3, the signature of a_i is B_S minus b_i and analogously b_i sees A_S minus a_i. Total domination forces a,b≥2; two outside vertices have equal nonempty signatures precisely when two matching indices are fully unrepresented, so t≤1. Four index states 1,x,y,xy give the bivariate all-set enumerator Π_{a,b≥2}[(x+y+xy)^n+n(x+y+xy)^{n-1}]. Multinomial coefficients and inclusion-exclusion yield the stated univariate expression (restore 6z² at n=3). Deleting a suitable selected endpoint from a doubled index, or from one of ≥3 singly represented vertices when t=0, proves every inclusion-minimal feasible set has minimum size max(4,n-1); exact counts 9,30,n(2^{n-1}-2n) for n=3,4,≥5 respectively. Explicit minimum constructions cover all n≥3.
risks: LTD compares open-neighborhood intersections only for vertices outside S; changing to metric locating, locating-dominating (not total) or identifying codes changes the theorem.

evidence: The four-state feasibility criterion and exact polynomial support future counting/optimization on a natural matching-deleted bipartite graph family.
value.rationale: Crown graphs are a canonical infinite family (K_n×K_2). The theorem counts every labeled locating-total dominating set by side sizes, identifies all inclusion-minimal solutions and proves the unusual rigidity that minimum and inclusion-minimal coincide. This is a natural complete invariant classification rather than a small arbitrary sample.
risks: Applies only to a full deleted perfect matching with n≥3; does not apply to metric resolving sets or arbitrary partial-match deletions.
